speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) whether the Ministry is able to do more to limit the number of +65 scam calls made to unsuspecting Singaporeans; and (b) whether the Ministry and local telcos can expand its scam awareness outreach efforts offline particularly to the elderly who have no knowledge of such apps.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: One key initiative, which the Member cited is our effort to combat scam phone calls from overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The technological solutions that we implement need to be complemented by measures to heighten the awareness and vigilance of the public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The Government has also partnered key stakeholders like the National Crime Prevention Council (NCPC), banks and telcos to disseminate anti-scam messages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: These efforts take place online and offline, in order to reach out to a wider audience, including vulnerable segments in our society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The NCPC’s crime prevention ambassadors also reach out to seniors to share crime prevention tips at various community events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: A vigilant public remains critical in our defence against scams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: We urge members of the public to join in the fight against scams by looking out for family members and for one another.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I believe many Members in this House have asked this question about the +65 scam calls.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first question I have is, I have been receiving a lot of questions from residents about the +65 scam calls and it seems that the trend has increased quite significantly.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But we will continue our efforts and we are as concerned as the Member.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: As far as education, indeed, that is the key.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: In this, the education and outreach is not confined only to the specifics of a scam call or a spoof call, as our general efforts to education the public around using online technologies, digital technologies – which are often what the scam calls are trying to extract value from; as people have a comfort and understanding about those things; they will become more vigilant, more understanding about what is possible and what needs to be protected in this space.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We thank all stakeholders in our community who have helped to spread the word on this.
